sentences.text: Shuvuuia measured about 1 meter in length and weighed approximately 3.5 kilograms.
The animal possessed long, slender hindlimbs with short toes that likely allowed for significant running speed.
It also possessed unusually short but powerfully built forelimbs.
Newer specimens reveal that Shuvuuia had a massively enlarged thumb plus reduced second and third fingers, contrary to earlier beliefs of a single digit.
A Shuvuuia fossil was found surrounded by tube-like structures resembling the central shafts of modern bird feathers.
Biochemical analysis of feather-like structures on a Shuvuuia specimen confirmed it likely possessed a coat of feathers.
Shuvuuia was the fourth non-avian dinosaur to show direct evidence of feathers.
The genus name Shuvuuia comes from the Mongolian word for bird.
The genus Shuvuuia was described by Chiappe, Norell, and Clark in 1998.
Shuvuuia likely used its strong forelimbs to open insect nests and its mobile jaws to probe for prey.
Shuvuuia belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae, known for short, powerful forelimbs specialized for digging.
Shuvuuia fossils are found in the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia, dating to about 75 million years ago during the late Campanian.
Shuvuuia lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.

A 2025 study rejected the hypothesis that Shuvuuia had owl-like hearing, arguing that the measurement method compared braincase depths that differ significantly between basal theropods and modern birds.
